items.title: Introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway
items.summary: AI is now used in every part of a business, and as a result, companies send source code, customer records, and regulated data through inference providers. The assurance that no data is retained after processing is still publicly unverified. Payment platforms, cloud infrastructure, and most other layers that handle data this sensitive have a way to prove their controls to outside parties, and inference will follow the same path.Today we are introducing Audited ZDR on AI Gateway. A provider is labeled Audited ZDR only after an independent security firm tests its zero data retention claims against its code, infrastructure, and live traffic, then publishes the report. , , and  are launch partners that have already begun audits, and more providers are encouraged to join to help raise the bar for security and privacy. BasetenModalWaferAudited ZDR builds on two steps we took toward stronger governance earlier this year:We are now asking inference providers for the same thing we asked of ourselves: independent verification.ZDR guarantees rely on contracts and self-attestation. A provider agrees not to retain prompts or completions, and customers take that commitment on faith.For teams sending proprietary code, customer information, or regulated data through models, self-reported ZDR contracts don't provide enough assurance. Answering these questions means running a bespoke security review for every provider and the models they host. An audit answers them in public.To qualify for Audited ZDR on AI Gateway, an inference provider engages an independent security firm, chosen from among respected third-party auditors, to run the audit. The firm then tests the provider's zero data retention policy across the serving path for every model, endpoint, feature, and tool that handles AI Gateway traffic.The audit confirms that customer data is never written or retained on durable storage in any system. Customer data means prompts, completions, system prompts, embeddings, files, images and audio, tool and function-call payloads, and any derived data that could identify them. Coverage spans request logs, traces, metrics, crash dumps, prompt caches, abuse monitoring, analytics, backups, support tools, and training, fine-tuning, and evaluation datasets. The audit confirms that once a response is returned to AI Gateway, that content is deleted from the inference provider's systems. Where a request uses caching, such as a KV cache, the cache stays in volatile storage only for the period of the request, and is never written to durable storage. The audit requires this behavior to be disclosed.The audit also confirms: Auditors verify this by reviewing the inference provider's serving-path source code and infrastructure configuration, then running live tests. They send marked prompts through AI Gateway and search the provider's logging, caching, and storage systems for any trace of them.Every passing provider publishes the report under the auditor's name. It covers scope, methodology, dates, findings, and fix status, with any exceptions disclosed and redactions limited to exploit detail. AI Gateway links directly to the report.An independent audit checks a provider's code and infrastructure at a point in time, but production systems change. To add a detection layer between independent audits, Vercel also runs  against inference providers on AI Gateway.canary auditsEach run sends prompts containing unique, unindexed URLs mapped privately to a provider, model, and run. Because a ZDR provider should never retain, inspect, or crawl prompt content, any request to a canary URL triggers an investigation into the provider and model involved. Canary checks cannot detect prompts written to disk and never read, so they complement independent code and infrastructure audits rather than replacing them.We are adding an independently Audited ZDR provider tier and a team-wide toggle in AI Gateway policy settings. When enabled, AI Gateway routes and fails over your team's requests only across providers with published audits that meet the bar.Launch partners have started their audits, and each provider enters the tier as soon as its report is published. Launch partner reports are expected to be published by December 9, 2026.AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries and failover for higher uptime than connecting to providers directly. It reflects provider pricing with no markup and charges no platform fee on inference, including Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests. Read the  to get started.AI Gateway documentationThe audited tier works alongside AI Gateway's other compliance controls.  pins where a provider runs inference to the US, EU, Australia, or Japan, per request or team-wide, and any data the provider stores at rest stays in that region. items.title: Choose AI Gateway providers by headquarters country
items.summary: sends your  requests only to providers headquartered in countries you choose, so you can meet compliance and procurement rules about where your AI vendors are located.Provider headquartersAI GatewayYou can configure provider headquarters to be an allowlist of the countries to use, or a denylist of the countries to block. AI Gateway skips providers in blocked countries and routes requests to the rest of the list, so a model stays accessible as long as it is available in one of its allowed provider locations.
